title: Gauda Badi Khela
summary: An Odisha stick dance of the Gopal cattle-herding communities, performed in groups in the spring season, with short sticks struck together in rhythm.
howToPlay: Four hands rise from below, each holding a long cane. Four places are lit: the left pair, the middle pair, the right pair, and all four together.
Strike the place a closing ring marks, on the beat, so those canes meet in the air.
Keep a steady count: the pattern repeats as the game goes round.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and an extra stroke costs points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: Twelve to twenty-four men in matching dress dance in teams under captains, each holding two short sticks and striking the sticks of their neighbours in rhythm to a song, with friendly contests between groups.
credits: Tradition: gauda badi khela of Odisha; patterns written for this game
